tasks.title: BroadcastNestedLoopJoin in the Plan

description.context: GridUnion's Tariffs team maintains a slowly-changing tariff table where each row has valid_from and valid_to timestamps. Billing must join 850M meter readings to the right tariff for each reading's date — a range join, not an equi-join. A teammate shows you the .explain() output and asks you to identify the operator, the cost characteristics, and whether this is the right strategy.
description.task: What does BroadcastNestedLoopJoin tell you about cost, and what is the strategic implication for GridUnion?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
tariff_history is 4M rows (10 years of daily tariff changes per customer_type). The join condition is a non-equi range expression on date BETWEEN valid_from AND valid_to plus an equi-condition on customer_type. The plan shows BroadcastNestedLoopJoin.

Left Size: 850M rows

Right Size: 4M rows (~280MB compressed)

Join Condition: date BETWEEN valid_from AND valid_to AND meters.customer_type = tariff_history.customer_type

evidence.label: snippet.py
evidence.content:
result = meters.join(
    tariff_history,
    (meters.customer_type == tariff_history.customer_type) &
    (meters.date >= tariff_history.valid_from) &
    (meters.date <= tariff_history.valid_to),
    how='inner'
)
result.explain()

fields.label: What does BroadcastNestedLoopJoin tell you about cost, and what is the strategic implication for GridUnion?
options: BroadcastNestedLoopJoin appears whenever a join condition mixes equi and non-equi predicates; Spark splits the join into two phases, equi-joining first via BroadcastHashJoin then filtering by the range. The cost is the equi-join's O(m + n) plus the per-row filter, which scales linearly. The strategic implication is range joins are no more expensive than equi-joins at this scale

BroadcastNestedLoopJoin is Spark's optimized range-join operator that uses interval trees on the broadcast side; the cost is O(m + n log n) where the log factor comes from the interval-tree lookup per left row. The strategic implication is that range joins scale well as long as the broadcast side fits in driver memory, which it does at 4M rows

BroadcastNestedLoopJoin compares every left row against every right row on each executor — O(left × right) per executor, not O((m+n) log m) of sort-merge. With 4M tariff rows broadcast and 850M meter rows distributed, each executor compares its meter shard against all 4M tariff rows. Cost scales as left × right, so tariff growth produces large runtime increases

BroadcastNestedLoopJoin is Spark's last-resort operator when no equi-join key exists; the cost is O(m × n) globally, not per executor, because the join cannot be parallelized. The strategic implication is that range joins must be rewritten to use equi-joins (e.g., by pre-computing a date_key on each side) before they reach production scale
fields.correctAnswer: BroadcastNestedLoopJoin compares every left row against every right row on each executor — O(left × right) per executor, not O((m+n) log m) of sort-merge. With 4M tariff rows broadcast and 850M meter rows distributed, each executor compares its meter shard against all 4M tariff rows. Cost scales as left × right, so tariff growth produces large runtime increases
fields.rationale: Nested loops over the broadcast side are exactly what the operator does. The cost is O(left × right) per executor — distinctly worse than sort-merge's O((m+n) log m). At GridUnion scale, 850M meter rows × 4M tariff rows is 3.4 quadrillion comparisons, distributed across executors but still dominated by the inner loop.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Invents a two-phase equi-then-filter split. Spark uses one operator (BroadcastNestedLoopJoin) that evaluates the entire condition row-by-row.

Option B: Invents an interval-tree implementation. BroadcastNestedLoopJoin is a literal nested loop; no tree structure is built on the broadcast side.

Option D: Over-states cost as global. The cost is per-executor; parallelism reduces wall-clock time but not total comparisons.

tasks.title: Range-Join Skew Across Regions

description.context: GridUnion's nightly billing pipeline ran in 45 minutes for two years. After last quarter, the median runtime climbed to 3 hours despite no code changes. Investigation reveals the issue lives in the range join from PJSS2.1. Spark UI shows 198 of 200 tasks completing in ~3 minutes; two tasks run for 2.5 hours each. Per-task shuffle-read sizes are roughly equal — the skew is not in shuffle volume but in compute time. Both slow tasks process meter rows from the NORTH region. The Tariffs team owns tariff_history; the Billing team owns the pipeline. You diagnose what changed and which team needs to act.
description.task: What is the architectural diagnosis, which team's contract clause is at stake, and what is the appropriate cross-team resolution?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
GridUnion has 30 regions across 4 countries. NORTH region (Northern Europe) tariffs are typically updated quarterly. Last quarter, the Tariffs team merged a regulatory archive into tariff_history that added historical rows back to 2014 — but only for NORTH (the EU regulatory archive's source region). Other regions' tariff_history rows remain at typical 6-month valid intervals. The two slow tasks process meter rows partitioned to NORTH on customer_type.

Regions: 30 regions across 4 countries

Tariff History Change: NORTH had 12 years of regulatory tariff history merged in last quarter; valid intervals span 2014–2026 instead of 6-month windows

Ownership Billing Team: owns the pipeline, the SLA, the join code

Ownership Tariffs Team: owns tariff_history schema and data freshness

Incident Runtime Before: 45 minutes

Incident Runtime After: 3 hours, P50; 2.5h on the two NORTH-region tasks

fields.label: What is the architectural diagnosis, which team's contract clause is at stake, and what is the appropriate cross-team resolution?
options: Diagnosis: NORTH meter rows triggered the slow tasks; the cause is the tariff_history valid_interval explosion — Tariffs team's recent merge expanded NORTH's intervals from ~6 months to 12 years. BroadcastNestedLoopJoin compares each NORTH meter row against ALL NORTH tariff rows (now ~50× more in the relevant slice). Resolution requires both teams: Tariffs adds a max-interval-cardinality contract clause; Billing partitions the range join by region so per-region explosions are bounded; both add per-region monitoring

Diagnosis: the NORTH partitions hit a Catalyst optimizer regression introduced in a Spark version upgrade last quarter; the optimizer no longer pushes the customer_type filter into BroadcastNestedLoopJoin, forcing a full scan of tariff_history per left row regardless of customer_type. The fix is internal: Billing pins the Spark version until the regression is patched, and the Platform team raises a Spark issue with the upstream community for resolution

Diagnosis: the slow tasks are the result of disk-cache eviction on the executors holding NORTH partitions; tariff_history was previously cached in memory but recent cluster-wide memory pressure from other teams' new pipelines evicted the broadcast. Resolution: Billing adds .persist(MEMORY_AND_DISK) to tariff_history before the join, restoring the cache and resolving the runtime regression without any cross-team coordination needed

Diagnosis: NORTH meter rows have null customer_type at higher rates than other regions (a known Junior-bug pattern in NORTH's source meter feed); the null-key drop is producing a Cartesian-product-like fan-out where Spark evaluates every NORTH meter against every tariff_history row to confirm no match exists. Resolution: Billing filters null customer_type before the join; this is a correctness fix that incidentally resolves the runtime regression because the slow path is no longer triggered
fields.correctAnswer: Diagnosis: NORTH meter rows triggered the slow tasks; the cause is the tariff_history valid_interval explosion — Tariffs team's recent merge expanded NORTH's intervals from ~6 months to 12 years. BroadcastNestedLoopJoin compares each NORTH meter row against ALL NORTH tariff rows (now ~50× more in the relevant slice). Resolution requires both teams: Tariffs adds a max-interval-cardinality contract clause; Billing partitions the range join by region so per-region explosions are bounded; both add per-region monitoring
fields.rationale: BroadcastNestedLoopJoin's cost scales as left × right per executor (PJSS2.1 covered this). The Tariffs team's recent merge added 12 years of historical NORTH tariffs with valid intervals spanning 2014–2026 instead of typical 6-month windows. For NORTH meters, the inner loop now iterates over ~50× more rows than before — and only NORTH partitions are affected because the regulatory archive only contains NORTH data. The 198 non-NORTH tasks see no change.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option B: Reaches for a 'Spark version regression' explanation. The data signature (only NORTH affected, scaled with the recent merge) is data-driven, not engine-driven.

Option C: Reaches for a cache-eviction explanation. Cache eviction would affect all regions equally, not just NORTH.

Option D: Confuses null-key drop with range-join cost explosion. Null-key drops produce row loss, not slow tasks; the symptom does not match.
